LESSON: NULLIFIERS OF SAUM (FASTING)

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
Strand: Devotional Acts 4.
Topic 4.1: Nullifiers of Saum (fasting)
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Nullifiers of Saum (fasting), part of Devotional Acts 4. in Grade 5 ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION.

Key inquiry question: Why should Muslims observe rules and regulation when fasting? 2. What virtues do Muslims learn from fasting?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. discuss the nullifiers of saum and make presentation in class,

2. sort nullifiers of saum from conditions of saum on flash cards,

3. brainstorm on rules and regulations of saum and make class presentation. 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. discuss the nullifiers of saum and make presentation in class,
2. sort nullifiers of saum from conditions of saum on flash cards,
3. brainstorm on rules and regulations of saum and make class presentation. 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Nullifiers of Saum (fasting) together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Critical thinking and problem solving: the skill of creativity as learners sort nullifiers of saum from conditions of saum on

flash cards.

• Communication and collaboration: the skills of listening, speaking and teamwork enhanced as learners discuss the nullifiers

of saum and make presentation in class.

Values:
Respect is inculcated during group discussion as learners appreciate diverse opinions.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Empathy as leaners observe saum by thinking about the learners/people who don’t have food.

Links to other Learning Areas:
Languages: Arabic and English as learners acquire new vocabularies as they discuss the

nullifiers of saum.
